evidence.note: Read run_tests.sh/test scripts and utils.py, obtained per-suite test counts, sampled all three suites, and inspected filter.json to learn which tests are actually scored — establishing what the corpus demands before coding.

Systematically characterized hard cases: counted WACC chapters, hunted advanced/hardest WACC tests, doubles, hard floats, bitfields, total complexity, and checked gcc/as/ld availability — deriving feature scope/priority from evidence (anchor 8).

Sustained drilling into specific ABI/semantics corners when classes of tests failed: bitfield layout, struct argument passing/return, stack alignment — inspecting emitted assembly to build a precise model of each corner.

Throughout the horizon, treated the suites as an evolving spec: on each failure, read the exact C source (zero-struct, bitfld, nestfunc, statement-expr) and reference behavior, then fed understanding back into codegen/parser fixes (anchor 10 behavior).

reasoning: The opening (steps 3-40) is a thorough, evidence-driven characterization of run_tests.sh, the scored test set, and the distribution of hard features (structs, doubles, bitfields, preprocessor), matching anchor 8, and tool availability was confirmed.
